top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a mature, independently reproduced capability: the magic-wavelength trap cancels the light shift by design, 1e-18 uncertainties have been cross-checked between laboratories, and the clocks now measure new physics (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on varying constants and dark matter). It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and the two-name allocation is clean. P002 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene) is a real discovery with a tested prediction, but the pairing mechanism is open, the field is young and the three-name credit omits Cao and others, so it ranks second. No award is last because both proposals are scientifically prize-worthy.
recusal_note: No specific conflict with any proposed laureate; I am a close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and of Lund and ETH attosecond groups, and work in adjacent atomic physics, but none of this involves Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer.
